title: Give web viewer navigation stable URLs so reload keeps your place
body:
Problem
The web viewer has no URLs for navigation. On load app.js reads the access token from the link's fragment, stores it in sessionStorage and replaces the address with a bare "/" (src/task_mcp/viewer_assets/app.js lines 5-7). The address never reflects where the user is, so reloading forgets the location (the token survives in sessionStorage), and back/forward and bookmarks do not work.

Required behavior
- Every navigable location has a stable URL: at least the selected project, the view (a named workstream, all tasks, task groups or a specific group) and the selected task.
- Reloading restores that location. Browser back/forward moves between locations visited in the viewer. A copied or bookmarked URL opens the same location in a session that already holds the token.
- The access token never appears in these URLs; the existing token-in-fragment launch link keeps working and then switches to the location URL.
- Unknown or stale locations (for example a deleted task or workstream) fall back gracefully to the nearest valid view with a short notice, not an error page.
- Route scheme (hash or path routing) is the implementer's choice; if path routing is used, the local server must serve the app for those paths without loosening its access checks.
- Navigation actions that exist today (workstream links, group chips, task selection, project choice) update the URL; in-progress features such as drag-and-drop reordering keep working.
- Update docs/viewer.md and README where they describe launching or navigating the viewer.

Related
tsk_06264e27ae5a4e02a99b056aefe04079 (GUI review/direction design) may change viewer controls later; stable URLs should not depend on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reloading the page on any project, workstream, all-tasks, task-groups or group view, with or without a selected task, returns to the same place.
- Back/forward follow viewer navigation; a bookmarked location URL reopens it in a tab that holds the token.
- No location URL contains the access token; the launch link still works.
- Stale or unknown locations fall back to a valid view with a notice.
- Verified in a real browser on a disposable database; repository tests and gates pass; independent review before user sign-off.
